This head unit's battery page may be rejected as "multimedia not supported" (common on BYD DiLink). Set WindTone manually via any path below (path 1 first on head units):

1) App start management → WindTone → Allow auto-start / Allow background running (common DiLink entry)
2) Settings → Apps → WindTone → Power management → Allow background activity
3) Settings → Battery → App power management → WindTone → Unrestricted
4) Settings → Apps → WindTone → Battery → Not optimised / Allow background

If none exists it still works: as long as the accessibility service or Usage access is on, app switches stay accurate. The allow-list only protects against being frozen after a long standby.

On Song L DM-i (incl. 2026 / DiLink 100) accessibility is often under vehicle settings. Try:
1) Vehicle settings → System → Accessibility → Downloaded / Installed services → WindTone (on) 2) Settings → System → Accessibility → Downloaded services → WindTone 3) Settings → Apps → Special app access → Accessibility 4) Settings → Accessibility (sometimes at the bottom)
To keep it usable: · Also enable Usage access (About & diagnostics → Foreground app log) — DiLink usually keeps this across reboot · App info → WindTone → allow autostart / background if present · Battery unrestricted whitelist so polling survives screen-off

Always on via Media3 single-player continuous queue; tracks with encoder delay/padding play without gaps

WindTone uses one ExoPlayer (Media3) with a continuous MediaItem queue. Media3 reads per-track encoder delay/padding and joins album splits without an audible gap when metadata is present.

There is no Media3 API to turn this off. Forcing gaps would mean inserting silence between tracks, which we deliberately do not do.

Lyrics are read from .lrc / .krc / .yrc files next to the audio first, then from embedded tags.\nThere is exactly one network feature: Check for updates / Download new version contacts the public distribution repository on GitHub (LuckyLearning/Release; it tries the official address first, falls back to third-party mirrors, and can be pinned in Download route). No data is collected or uploaded.

How lyrics are found:
1. Sidecar in the same Aliyun Drive folder (.lrc / .krc / .yrc / .txt)
2. Same-named lyric file next to the audio
3. Embedded lyrics (MP3 USLT/SYLT, FLAC/Ogg LYRICS, M4A ©lyr)
4. Lyrics from a same-named track in the local library (local only; no online search)

If a cloud track has none of the above, this hint is shown as-is. Put a same-named lyric file in the cloud folder, or add the song to the local library.
